facts.statement: Diplodoselache was an extinct cartilaginous fish that lived during the Carboniferous period in Scotland and possibly Russia.
facts.quote: Diplodoselache is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish from the Carboniferous of Scotland and possibly Russia.

facts.statement: John Dick described the genus Diplodoselache in 1981 using four complete skeletons found in Viséan-stage ironstone concretions.
facts.quote: Diplodoselache was described by John Dick in 1981 based on four complete skeletons preserved in Viséan-stage ironstone concretions.

facts.statement: The type species Diplodoselache woodi honors Stan Wood, who found the first complete fossils in Scotland's Midland Valley region.
facts.quote: The type species, D. woodi, is named in honor of Scottish fossil collector Stan Wood, who discovered the first complete fossils of the species in the Midland Valley region of Scotland.

facts.statement: Diplodoselache possessed a single dorsal fin with a spine similar to those found on the heads of other xenacanthiform fishes.
facts.quote: It had a single dorsal fin, which supported a fin spine that was similar to those on the back of the head in other xenacanthiform fishes.

facts.statement: The largest complete Diplodoselache specimen measured 1.12 meters, though Dick suggested some individuals may have been considerably larger than one meter.
facts.quote: The largest complete specimen is 1.12 meters in length, but in Dick's description of the taxon he suggests some individuals were "considerably greater than one metre" in length.

facts.statement: Diplodoselache is classified within the xenacanth family Diplodoselachidae.
facts.quote: The genus is placed in the xenacanth family Diplodoselachidae.

facts.statement: Diplodoselache was a predator that lived in lagoonal environments.
facts.quote: Diplodoselache was a predator which inhabited a lagoonal environment.

facts.statement: Diplodoselache lived between 339.9 and 335.9 million years ago during the Visean stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Visean (339.9 to 335.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Diplodoselache teeth featured two large outer cusps and one very small inner cusp.
